text: Plant room fitters stripping a circulation pump union often work with a few inches of swing, and the sliding jaw lets the plier be set on the nut before the handle is squeezed, so a drain-down is finished before the system refills.
Second-fix electricians terminating a row of back boxes can strip, twist and cut with the cable already clipped in the wall, so a room is closed up in one visit without carrying the tails to a bench.

Kitchen fitters adjusting hinge plates after the doors are hung can reach the screws inside a carcass with the compact gun body, so a final alignment pass is finished without swapping to a hand driver.

Mobile engravers working a market stall or an event stand can mark pet tags and gifts on the spot, since the cordless body needs no socket at the table and the kit packs back into its case between venues.
Sheet metal shops can deburr punched holes and dressed edges at the bench with a mounted stone, so a batch of brackets is cleaned before powder coating instead of being filed by hand.

Small engine shops servicing mowers and brushcutters can run the deck and casing bolts off with the compact head, so a machine is stripped, serviced and reassembled between its drop-off and collection.
Body shops stripping interiors can run seat frame and seat belt anchor bolts out from inside the cabin, where the right-angle head clears the centre console and the trim stays in place.

Agricultural contractors servicing trailers and spreaders between fields can take the cased set to the implement, so a worn linkage bolt is changed in the yard instead of towing the machine to a workshop.
Shopfitters building a lift-up counter return can hold the flap open while serving and lower it at close, so a small kiosk gets a service hatch without a leg or a stay to catch on.
Households using a spare room as a study can fold the shelf up against the wall when the desk is cleared, so the room returns to a bedroom without unscrewing a fixed shelf.
Locksmiths and door fitters can add the viewer while a door is already off its hinges for a lock change, saving a separate visit and leaving the flat secured the same day.
Vinyl and window film installers can trim a sheet back along the frame with the blade set shallow, so the edge is cut clean against the gasket without scoring the glass underneath.
Suspended ceiling and partition crews can cut hanger wire and stud ties at the grid, so a tile line or a stud run is adjusted from below without a trip down the ladder for a larger cutter.
Compressed air fitters running a line through a workshop can change jaw size at each coupling without leaving the ladder, so a drop is piped and pressure-tested in a single pass.

Renovation carpenters cutting out a rotten sill can run the blade into the reveal where a circular saw cannot reach, so a repair section is removed and replaced in one visit without dismantling the whole frame.
Riser cupboards and lofts often have no light fitting, so a lamp kept in the tool bag means a fault is traced on the first visit instead of a return with a lead light
Importers can ship the grinder with a starter burr assortment, so a shop ordering its first air tool takes the head and the cutters it needs in one line
Chipping slag and spatter off a welded frame keeps the next jig load sitting flat, so a fabrication bay cleans between passes instead of stacking work on a rough surface
Sewing and craft rooms can use a drop leaf as extra work surface that folds away, so a small room holds a full-size table only while a project is out
A fitter replacing two damaged pulls can buy just those two, so an open-stock line covers small repairs without a sealed pack going into a van as dead stock
Sites can put the same 10 mm ratchet in every technician tool roll, so a worn or missing wrench is replaced from one part number instead of a matched set
Scaffolders and groundworkers can twist and cut tie wire with the jaws, so a tying run is completed without a second pair of pliers on the belt
Garden and irrigation fitters can pull and cut the wire ties on a dripper line with the short jaws, so a repair is made without unclipping the whole run
Roofers and gutter cleaners can blow moss and grit along a gutter run from the ladder, so a clearance job is finished without a bucket and trowel
